blocks.prompt: 5. The \(18^{\text{th}}\) term of a sequence is 367. The \(30^{\text{th}}\) term of the sequence is 499. How many terms of this sequence are less than 1000?
blocks.explanation:
The sequence is an A.P. (this is the A.P. exercise), and two of its terms are known.
We must count the terms below 1000.
Plan: two equations give \(a_1\) and \(d\); then solve \(a_n < 1000\) for the largest whole \(n\).
steps:
Given: \(a_{18} = 367,\ a_{30} = 499\) (an A.P.)
To find: the number of terms with \(a_n < 1000\).
Method: Write both terms with \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\), subtract to find \(d\), then \(a_1\). The terms increase, so all terms up to some \(n\) are below 1000.

Write the two equations
\[a_1 + 17d = 367 \quad (1)\]
\[a_1 + 29d = 499 \quad (2)\]
Why: The 18th term is \(a_1\) plus 17 steps; the 30th is \(a_1\) plus 29 steps.

Subtract to find \(d\), then \(a_1\)
\[(2) - (1):\ 12d = 132\]
\[d = 11\]
\[a_1 = 367 - 17(11) = 367 - 187 = 180\]
Why: Subtracting removes \(a_1\). Then put \(d = 11\) back in (1).

Solve the inequality
\[11n + 169 < 1000\]
\[11n < 831\]
\[n < 75.5\]
Why: \(831 \div 11 = 75.54\ldots\). \(n\) must be a whole number, so the largest possible \(n\) is 75.

Check the border terms
\[a_{75} = 11(75) + 169 = 994 < 1000\]
\[a_{76} = 1005 > 1000\]
Why: Since \(d > 0\) the terms keep increasing, so exactly \(a_1, \ldots, a_{75}\) are below 1000.
